page: Amazon Web Services c5d.large is a compute-optimized server instance operating on the hardware-assisted AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It features a single physical Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz, exposing 2 dedicated virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. System memory comprises 4.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, resulting in a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Storage features a direct-attached 50 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network performance is rated at 1 Gbps, and CPU capabilities include vector and cryptographic instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES, and FMA.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate moderate single-thread compute capabilities paired with lower multi-thread performance due to the two-vCPU core ceiling. In stress-ng benchmarks, single-core performance achieved a score of 1484.88, while multi-core throughput recorded 1953.77. Uncached memory read bandwidth recorded 12.85 GB/sec and uncached memory write bandwidth recorded 11.51 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks showed Redis SET performance at 1.8 million operations per second, static web serving throughput at 2.06 GB/sec, and 135M parameter LLM prompt processing at 117.52 tokens per second.

The c5d.large combines entry-level dedicated processing resources with local high-speed NVMe storage. The direct-attached SSD provides low-latency disk access without network storage latency overhead. However, memory bandwidth and total capacity are limited by the 4.0 GB RAM footprint, restricting use cases that require large in-memory databases or parallel execution. This configuration is suitable for entry-level batch processing, microservices, local caching layers, and lightweight web serving workloads requiring scratch storage access.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.large is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8124M processor delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core. Equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a direct-attached 50 GB NVMe SSD, the server offers low-latency local storage coupled with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth on the AWS Nitro system. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512, AES, and FMA. Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 1484.88, while multi-threaded tasks and uncached memory bandwidth fall in lower benchmark tiers due to the compact resource profile. The direct NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space, though total system RAM restricts memory-heavy deployments. The c5d.large is structured for entry-level compute tasks, small batch jobs, microservices, and lightweight web processing requiring high-speed local disk access.
